title: Projective constructibility from projective-line constructibility
statement:
Suppose $\mathcal C(\mathbf P^1_T\to T)$ holds for every
finite-type $k$-scheme $T$. Then $\mathcal C(f)$ holds for
every projective morphism $f:X\to S$ between finite-type
$k$-schemes, using the conventions of
[def-finrepair-property-c], [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions].
Here projective has the closed-embedding convention of [def-pc-projective-morphism].

proof.text: Use the supplied closed embedding e:X→ℙ(N;S) with f=e≫p, as in [def-pc-projective-morphism]. The index N is finite and is allowed to be empty. It suffices to prove C(e) and C(p), then apply [lem-finrepair-composition-c].

source.place: Proof; source-library implementation in F1 Projective delivery

proof.text: The structure projection of every finite-coordinate projective space is proper by [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper]. Thus its composites with a finite-type map to Spec k are finite type, using [def-weil-proper-morphism] and [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Over the Noetherian field k, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes S and ℙ(N;S) Noetherian. These instances suffice for the finite-surjection cancellation and for the quasi-compactness of open complements of closed immersions.

source.place: Proof; source-library implementation in F1 Projective delivery

proof.text: A closed immersion into a Noetherian scheme satisfies C: by [lem-fin-closed-immersion], its underived direct image of a constructible sheaf is constructible and its positive derived images vanish. Equivalently, exactness identifies its total derived image of F[0] with (e_*F)[0]; the latter has constructible homology by [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]. This proves C in [def-finrepair-property-c], and applies also to an identity and to a map from an empty scheme.

source.place: Proof; source-library implementation in F1 Projective delivery

proof.text: Define Z_0=S, Z_(m+1)=ℙ¹_(Z_m), with tower projection q_m:Z_m→S, using the base-change presentation [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]. Induction gives properness of every q_m from properness of projective-line projections [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper]. Consequently Z_m→Spec k is finite type. The identity case of Step 3 gives C(q_0). At the successor, the universally quantified hypothesis gives C(ℙ¹_(Z_m)→Z_m), and [lem-finrepair-composition-c] composes it with C(q_m). Hence C(q_m) for every m.

source.place: Proof; source-library implementation in F1 Projective delivery

proof.text: If N is nonempty, use the source-library form of [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-product-finite], namely ProjectiveSpace.exists_isFinite_surjective_projectiveLinePow: it supplies m and a finite surjective σ:Z_m→ℙ(N;S) with σ≫p=q_m. Unlike the older Noetherian wrapper, this existing proved declaration already handles arbitrary finite nonempty coordinate types and m=0. Apply [lem-finrepair-finite-surjection-cancellation] over the finite-type k-scheme ℙ(N;S) to the equality and Step 4, obtaining C(p). If N is empty, projective space is empty by its standard-open cover; p is then a closed immersion and Step 3 gives C(p) directly.

proof.text: Step 3 gives C(e) and Step 5 gives C(p). Apply [lem-finrepair-composition-c], then rewrite e≫p=f. This proves the stated projective reduction without imposing any coefficient exponent beyond the original finite-ring hypothesis.
